name: General Intuition
description: General Intuition is privately held and has no ticker. Review its funding rounds and valuations, the investors and SPVs that hold its shares, and the points to confirm before buying or selling.
ledes: General Intuition is a privately held artificial intelligence research company. Its shares are not listed on an exchange and have no quoted market price; the principal public reference points are the valuations at which the company has raised capital. Its most recent financing, a $220 million Series B round announced on September 29, 2026, valued the company at $6.2 billion.

Founded in 2025 and based in New York, General Intuition was spun out of Medal, a platform on which players share video game clips, and develops AI models, trained on gameplay footage, that learn to plan and act in simulated and physical environments. Existing shares change hands in privately negotiated transactions and remain subject to the company's transfer restrictions.
table_note: Valuations are post-money. The Series A was announced in June 2026; GamesBeat reported that the funding had been completed in January.
round_notes: No lead investor was named for the Series B. General Intuition states on its website that it has raised more than $650 million over the past year; that figure is the company's own.

A round valuation reflects the terms of the preferred stock issued in that round. Most shares sold by employees are common stock, which carries fewer rights and typically trades at a discount to the preferred price.
investors: Valor Equity Partners, Atreides, Point72 and Seven Seven Six joined existing investors Khosla Ventures and General Catalyst in the Series B. Khosla Ventures led the Series A, and Khosla Ventures and General Catalyst co-led the seed round. Other investors include Hedosophia, Raine, Jeff Bezos, Eric Schmidt and Nico Rosberg.
spv_sentence: SEC filings show two special purpose vehicles formed to invest in General Intuition, both organized in 2026.
sources: Sources: reports by TechCrunch (June 2026 and October 2025), SiliconANGLE (September 2026) and GamesBeat (June 2026); General Intuition's website; and SEC Form D filings.
